observations: Reference source invokes crypto/rand.Read with its default Reader and never installs testingReader, an alternate Reader, or deterministic bytes.

Current public Read dispatches to crypto/internal/fips140/drbg.Read in its default non-boring case; drbg.Read uses sysrand.Read when FIPS mode is disabled. Actual build/runtime mode has not been probed.
sysrand uses the Unix getrandom layer; that layer first tries runtime.vgetrandom, then a real syscall, and caches ENOSYS before the device fallback.
The Linux runtime supports kernel vDSO getrandom state. A nonempty SDK draw need not issue a syscall on every call; absent syscalls are not evidence of a seeded replacement.
uuid.NewV4 uses crypto/rand.Read for its actual payload; uuid.NewV7 uses actual time.Now, serialized state, then crypto/rand.Read on its random suffix.
